skill.name: backend-development-feature-development
skill.description: Orchestrate end-to-end backend feature development from requirements to deployment. Use when coordinating multi-phase feature delivery across teams and services.
skill.summary: Coordinate complex feature delivery from requirements through production rollout.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The only static finding is a false positive because SKILL.md line 35 requires approvals and rollback plans before production changes. No evidence of reconnaissance, prompt injection, exfiltration, or malicious intent was found.

static_findings.snippet: - Avoid production changes without approvals and rollback plans.

finding_verdicts.reason: SKILL.md line 35 is a defensive instruction to avoid production changes without approvals and rollback plans. It contains no system discovery, host enumeration, or reconnaissance behavior.

content.value_statement: Complex backend features often fail when requirements, architecture, testing, and rollout work remain disconnected. This skill coordinates twelve delivery phases with defined outputs, controls, and handoffs.
actual_capabilities: Transforms a feature brief into user stories, acceptance criteria, success metrics, dependencies, and risks.
Defines service boundaries, API contracts, data models, integration points, and security requirements.
Coordinates backend, frontend, and data implementation through specialized agents and shared phase context.
Plans unit, integration, end-to-end, performance, and security testing with measurable quality targets.
Prepares feature flags, gradual rollout, monitoring, rollback procedures, and production documentation.
Supports traditional, TDD, BDD, and DDD methodologies across four feature complexity levels.
limitations: Requires compatible specialist agents for the complete twelve-phase workflow.
Does not replace environment-specific testing, security review, or production approval.
Creates unnecessary overhead for small isolated changes and routine bug fixes.
Depends on clear scope, constraints, permissions, and success criteria from the user.

use_cases.title: Plan a Cross-Service Feature
use_cases.description: Turn a product request into requirements, architecture, ownership, dependencies, risks, and measurable delivery criteria.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Technical Implementation
use_cases.description: Align backend, frontend, and data work through shared contracts, staged outputs, and integrated testing.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Controlled Rollout
use_cases.description: Define deployment gates, feature flags, observability, rollback actions, and operational documentation before release.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Feature Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a medium backend feature for [feature]. Use TDD and feature flags. Define requirements, architecture, tests, rollout, monitoring, and rollback outputs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for one feature with clear boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Multiple Services
prompt_templates.prompt: Coordinate delivery of [feature] across [services]. Identify dependencies, API and data changes, ownership, security checks, acceptance criteria, and a canary deployment plan.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate delivery across several services and teams.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Domain Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a DDD workflow for [feature] in [domain]. Define bounded contexts, aggregates, contracts, migration stages, testing layers, observability, and rollback controls.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced domain design with staged implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Orchestrate an Epic Rollout
prompt_templates.prompt: Orchestrate an epic for [feature] across [teams and systems]. Include phased ownership, compliance gates, performance budgets, data migration, canary metrics, incident thresholds, and rollback decisions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced delivery with broad architectural and operational impact.

output_examples.input: Plan a payment retry feature using TDD and a canary rollout.
output: Requirements define retry eligibility, customer outcomes, acceptance criteria, and payment risk controls.
Architecture covers retry scheduling, idempotency, event contracts, failure handling, and audit records.
Testing includes unit, integration, end-to-end, performance, and payment security checks.
Rollout starts with limited traffic and monitors recovery rate, duplicate charges, latency, and errors.

output_examples.input: Coordinate account deletion across identity, billing, and analytics services.
output: The delivery plan assigns service ownership and defines deletion contracts, retention rules, and dependency order.
Migration and testing stages verify authorization, data removal, legal retention, and failure recovery.
Operational gates include audit evidence, monitoring, staged activation, and a tested rollback procedure.

output_examples.input: Prepare a feature-flag rollout for a new recommendation API.
output: The rollout begins with internal users, then expands through measured traffic stages.
Dashboards track latency, error rate, recommendation quality, feature usage, and business outcomes.
Automatic stop conditions and flag disable procedures provide immediate recovery.

best_practices: Provide current architecture, owners, constraints, and measurable success criteria before starting discovery.
Review each phase output before passing it to implementation or deployment agents.
Validate migrations, feature flags, monitoring, and rollback procedures in staging before production approval.
anti_patterns: Do not use the complete workflow for a small isolated fix.
Do not deploy generated changes without environment-specific testing and human approval.
Do not proceed when scope, permissions, safety boundaries, or success criteria remain unclear.

faq.question: What features fit this skill?
faq.answer: Use it for complex features spanning requirements, architecture, implementation, testing, deployment, monitoring, and documentation.

faq.question: Which development methods are supported?
faq.answer: The workflow supports traditional delivery, TDD, BDD, and DDD.

faq.question: Can it handle small bug fixes?
faq.answer: It can, but the full workflow adds unnecessary overhead. Use a focused specialist skill for small fixes.

faq.question: Does it deploy directly to production?
faq.answer: No. Production changes require explicit approvals, validated rollback plans, and environment-specific checks.

faq.question: Which rollout strategies are included?
faq.answer: It supports direct, canary, feature-flag, blue-green, and A/B test strategies.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the feature scope, methodology, complexity, constraints, architecture context, success metrics, and preferred deployment strategy.
